observations.summary: The report assigns approximately 7,140 square metres per gram to graphene.
The report attributes world-first roll-to-roll CVD methodology and defect-free large-area monolayers to the company.
The report describes a planar-heater cooker and claims better efficiency than conventional coils without measurement details.
The report links an 80°C exterior limit to absence of burns and describes holographic visuals.
The report gives 2012 as incorporation year and describes expansion toward consumer appliances and industrial supply chains.
The authors give a theoretical graphene-sheet surface area of 2,630 square metres per gram.
The authors report CVD growth and roll-to-roll handling of mostly monolayer 30-inch films; the publication predates the report’s stated 2012 company formation.

observations.locator: Publisher abstract, grain boundaries and transport results
observations.summary: The authors identify CVD graphene grain boundaries and report effects on electrical transport.

observations.locator: Product description: Precise temperature control; Thin and highly portable
observations.summary: The manufacturer distinguishes a front panel near 75°C/~200 W from a bottom panel near 400°C/~1 kW and describes an LCD-reflection visual arrangement.

observations.locator: Product description: Flexible structure and smart usability
observations.summary: The manufacturer advertises up to 30% power reduction but the inspected passage gives no matched task, baseline appliance, or uncertainty.
The guide makes allowable heated-surface conditions dependent on contact duration, surface configuration, and accepted injury level.

claims.text: The supplied original is a company-focused report on graphene synthesis and heating appliances, rather than a record of controlled appliance measurements.
claims.reasoning: The complete 43-line text summarizes properties, company technology, and products but contains no experimental protocol or raw measurements.
claims.counterargument: Images or another original revision could contain additional evidence.
claims.limitation: This classification covers the retrieved text export only; it does not establish the student’s actual activity.

claims.text: The report’s 7,140 m²/g figure should be corrected or justified against the conventional 2,630 m²/g ideal-sheet reference.
claims.reasoning: The reported value is about 2.715 times the reference; neither one-sided versus two-sided convention alone yields 7,140.
claims.counterargument: A different material, adsorption definition, or structured sample could require a different metric.
claims.limitation: The audit diagnoses a mismatch; it does not measure a sample or assert that every graphene-derived porous material has the same area.

claims.text: CVD processing alone does not justify a universal defect-free monolayer claim.

source_locators.locator: Publisher abstract, grain boundaries and transport results

claims.reasoning: A demonstrated CVD route can include boundaries that alter transport; a product claim needs mapped quality and yield evidence.
claims.counterargument: A particular advanced process might produce much higher-quality material than the cited samples.
claims.limitation: No Graphene Square specimen or current quality-control dataset has been tested here.

claims.text: The report’s world-first corporate attribution remains unresolved.
claims.reasoning: A 2010 roll-to-roll publication precedes the source’s 2012 incorporation date, requiring a distinction between inventor research, patents, and a later company.
claims.counterargument: Founders or licensed inventions can predate incorporation; the dates do not refute legitimate technology lineage.
claims.limitation: No exhaustive prior-art or ownership search was performed.

claims.text: No quantified cooker energy advantage is established by the supplied report or inspected marketing passage.

source_locators.locator: Product description: Flexible structure and smart usability

claims.reasoning: Thermal conductivity and planar geometry do not specify task-level electrical energy per matched outcome; power is not energy.
claims.counterargument: The product could save energy through geometry, control, insulation, or reduced heat loss.
claims.limitation: Absence of protocol in the inspected sources is not proof of no efficiency benefit.

claims.text: An 80°C figure alone cannot support elimination of contact-burn risk; the current radiator page also distinguishes multiple heating panels.

source_locators.locator: Product description: Precise temperature control; Thin and highly portable

claims.reasoning: Risk assessment needs exposure and construction context; one reported panel temperature cannot establish safety of the whole device.
claims.counterargument: The source may refer to another version or an inaccessible heating surface.
claims.limitation: This is a wording and evidence audit, not a product safety determination or certification.

claims.text: The radiator visual should be described as a manufacturer-reported optical display arrangement, not as graphene independently producing holograms.

source_locators.locator: Product description: Precise temperature control; Thin and highly portable

claims.reasoning: The manufacturer attributes the visual effect to an LCD-reflection assembly combined with transparent heating.
claims.counterargument: Marketing may use holographic for a perceived three-dimensional effect without formal wavefront reconstruction.
claims.limitation: Optical architecture and image quality have not been independently inspected.

claims.text: Industrial supply-chain expansion is an outlook statement in the supplied report, not a verified customer adoption result.
claims.reasoning: No named contract, shipment, or audited sales evidence accompanies this outlook in the source text.
claims.counterargument: Independent company disclosures could substantiate customer adoption later.
claims.limitation: No conclusion about actual commercial success or failure is drawn.

claims.text: Perform a matched-endpoint energy comparison only after student ownership, equipment access, and a safe supervised protocol are confirmed.
claims.reasoning: Task-level energy and repeatability can test a concrete efficiency claim.
claims.counterargument: Equipment availability may make a literature-only audit more appropriate.
claims.limitation: No physical test has been performed.

claims.text: For EC4–EC5 synthesis, compare evidence quality and claim boundaries before making cross-event technology trends.
claims.reasoning: Different source formats and companies create selection and date confounding.
claims.counterargument: A thematic qualitative comparison can still help if it explicitly preserves these differences.
